title: Hom reflection into internal principal cone outputs
statement: Fix a prime l, finite extension E/Q_l [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and scheme X. Work in the internal integral module category A and its derived category [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. Let d be an endomorphism of the regular condensed integral module whose action on every continuous function f on every profinite S is pointwise multiplication by the chosen uniformizer pi_E [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution]. Put mu_P=scalarOnComplex(d,P). For arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes P,Q in A, precomposition with Q(unit(mu_P)) induces a bijection Hom_D(Q(completion(mu_P)),Q(completion(mu_Q))) -> Hom_D(Q(P),Q(completion(mu_Q))), where completion and unit are the explicit principal mapping cocone constructions [def-pur-principal-cone-tower]. No K-flatness or termwise flatness is assumed.

source.place: Tags 099B (lemma-derived-completion) and 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941; the singleton case; coefficient regularity and the internal tower are as in sk-def-pe-derived-completion and det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution.

proof.text: Conjugate the pulled-back endomorphism d to an endomorphism of the tensor unit. The section-module equivalence sends its tensor action on a module to multiplication by the compatible section obtained by evaluating the unit endomorphism at one. Prove this on local pure tensors, using tensor naturality and the left-unitor formula. No regularity or identification with a constant uniformizer is needed for this reflection assertion.

Compose the section-module equivalence with direct restriction to the canonical AsSmall model. This is an additive equivalence. Pro-etale repleteness makes countable products exact in internal modules; transport that exactness to the small model. The principalCompletionMap comparison identifies each mapped completion and its actual unit with the completion of the mapped scalar.

On the small site represent the principal ideal as the image of multiplication by the scalar section. The singleton generating-list theorem applies also to zero or invertible scalars. Apply the ringed Koszul reflector, and compose the principal-cone/Koszul-Roos comparison with the strict Koszul presentation comparison for P and Q. Both comparisons preserve the specified augmentation. The reflector output for Q is complete, so its Hom bijection at P transfers to the two principal cone completions.

Transport the precomposition bijection back through the fully faithful derived equivalence. For injectivity, map two morphisms and cancel the comparison isomorphisms. For surjectivity, extend the mapped morphism by the small-site bijection, conjugate by the comparison isomorphisms, and take the full functor preimage. The derived localization factorization identifies the unit square.

proof_origin.place: Tags 099B and 0A0E, singleton image ideal; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941; normalized comparisons and exact section/small-model transport. R4 proves all assembly and scalar-identification steps without adding holes.

theorem internal_principal_cone_hom_reflection
    (d : End (Mod.regular (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E)))
    (hd : ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ) (f : (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E).obj.obj S)
      (s : S.unop), ((d.hom.hom.app S) f).down s =
        Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E * f.down s)
    (P Q : CochainComplex (Modules l E X) ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective (fun f :
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (CochainComplex.PrincipalCone.completion
        (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X d P)) ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (CochainComplex.PrincipalCone.completion
        (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X d Q)) ↦
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainComplex.PrincipalCone.unit
        (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X d P)) ≫ f)
